extracted.intended_audience: health communication professionals, public affairs/press officers, and program planners in cancer/public health agencies
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for planning, developing, implementing, and assessing health-related communication programs and for drafting patient-facing cancer press releases that follow NCI/National Plain Language standards. Emphasizes plain language, accurate risk communication, sourcing, accessibility, and coordination with government communications protocols.

rubrics_metrics.name: Stage 1: Planning and Strategy Development
rubrics_metrics.description: Define problem; Identify audiences; Set objectives; Assess organizational capabilities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Program planning stage: clearly define the communication problem to be addressed, segment and prioritize audiences, set measurable communication objectives, and assess whether organizational capacity and resources align with goals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Stage 2: Developing and Pretesting Concepts, Messages, and Materials
rubrics_metrics.description: Develop concept; Pretest with audience; Refine based on feedback; Develop draft materials; Pretest materials.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Iterative development: create conceptual approaches and messages, conduct formative/pretesting with intended audiences, use feedback to refine concepts and draft materials, and pretest final materials before full implementation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Stage 3: Implementing the Program
rubrics_metrics.description: Distribute materials; Engage partners; Monitor implementation; Address barriers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Implementation should include distribution planning, partnership engagement for reach, active monitoring of delivery and uptake, and troubleshooting/addressing barriers to reach and use.

rubrics_metrics.name: Stage 4: Assessing Effectiveness and Making Refinements
rubrics_metrics.description: Measure outcomes; Evaluate effectiveness; Refine for future programs; Document lessons.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use defined outcome measures and evaluation methods to assess whether objectives were met, apply findings to refine the program, and document lessons learned for future communication efforts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Plain Language Requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Plain Writing Act of 2010 mandates federal agencies write clearly; NCI uses Federal Plain Language Guidelines; health literacy considerations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow federal plain-language obligations: use clear, concise, well-organized writing that considers health literacy needs, avoiding unnecessary complexity and jargon.

rubrics_metrics.name: Patient-friendly language (Grade 6-8)
rubrics_metrics.description: Use patient-friendly language at approximately a 6th–8th grade reading level.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Write so that typical patients/readers can understand; prefer short sentences, common words, active voice, and explain unavoidable technical terms.

rubrics_metrics.name: Clear risk/benefit communication
rubrics_metrics.description: Communicate risks and benefits clearly to patients and the public.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Present both potential benefits and harms in balanced language; avoid overstating benefits or minimizing harms; include context to aid interpretation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use absolute numbers (not just relative)
rubrics_metrics.description: Prefer absolute risk/benefit numbers instead of only relative measures.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Report absolute rates (e.g., '2 of 1,000') alongside or instead of relative percentage changes to avoid misleading impressions of magnitude.

rubrics_metrics.name: Source credibility (peer-reviewed citations)
rubrics_metrics.description: Cite credible, peer-reviewed sources to support claims.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include references to peer-reviewed literature or authoritative sources; make provenance of findings clear to readers and journalists.

rubrics_metrics.name: Action steps for patients
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide clear next steps or recommended actions for affected populations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Tell readers what they can or should do (e.g., talk to their clinician, follow screening guidelines), making recommendations actionable and specific where appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Resources for more information
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide links or contacts for further reliable information and support.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include phone numbers, websites, patient resources, or referral information so readers can find more detailed guidance or support.

rubrics_metrics.name: Disclaimer about treatment decisions / appropriate caveats
rubrics_metrics.description: Include disclaimers that information is not a substitute for professional medical advice and caveats about study applicability.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explicitly state that press-release content does not replace clinician judgment, note that study findings may not directly translate into clinical recommendations, and caution about overgeneralization.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid disease-mongering
rubrics_metrics.description: Avoid language or framing that sensationalizes risk or exaggerates disease threats.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not use alarmist phrasing; frame findings responsibly and proportionately to the evidence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid 'cure' language without basis
rubrics_metrics.description: Do not claim a 'cure' or use cure-like language unless fully supported by evidence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be precise about outcomes and limitations; avoid implying definitive cures from preliminary or limited studies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Differentiate trial findings from approved treatments
rubrics_metrics.description: Clearly state whether results come from a clinical trial and are not equivalent to approved, standard treatments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Distinguish experimental interventions and trial-stage evidence from therapies that are approved and widely available; avoid conflating the two.

rubrics_metrics.name: Specify cancer type/stage
rubrics_metrics.description: Identify the specific cancer type and stage relevant to findings or recommendations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide specificity so readers understand the population to which results apply (e.g., tumor type, stage, demographic qualifiers).

rubrics_metrics.name: Include incidence/prevalence context
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide context about how common the disease or outcome is (incidence/prevalence).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Help readers judge the public-health significance by including baseline rates or population context.

rubrics_metrics.name: Distinguish from general claims
rubrics_metrics.description: Avoid broad or generalized claims not supported by the specific evidence presented.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be explicit about the study scope and limit claims to what the data support; avoid extrapolating beyond the evidence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Translate technical jargon
rubrics_metrics.description: Translate technical terms into plain-language equivalents for patient audiences.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When technical terms are necessary, define them in simple language or provide analogies; minimize unexplained jargon.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notes study limitations
rubrics_metrics.description: List and explain limitations of the study or evidence cited.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Discuss sample size, generalizability, follow-up time, confounders, and other methodological limitations so readers can assess reliability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Identifies funder
rubrics_metrics.description: Disclose the study funder(s) or sources of financial support.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include funding disclosures to allow readers to evaluate potential conflicts of interest or sponsor influence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provides accessible formats (alt text, etc.)
rubrics_metrics.description: Ensure press-release materials are available in accessible formats such as alt text for images and other accommodations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide alternative text for visuals, captioning/transcripts for multimedia, and other accessible formats to meet diverse needs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Includes mental health/support resources
rubrics_metrics.description: Include information about mental-health and support resources where appropriate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When content may provoke distress or affect patients, provide contacts for counseling, support groups, hotlines, or other resources.

rubrics_metrics.name: Coordinates with NIH/HHS communications protocol
rubrics_metrics.description: Coordinate messaging and timing with NIH/HHS communications protocols as appropriate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow interagency clearance or coordination procedures, and align messaging with relevant federal partners when required.

rubrics_metrics.name: Distinguishes individual benefit from population effect
rubrics_metrics.description: Clarify whether reported benefits apply to individuals or populations and explain differences.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explain absolute versus relative effects and make clear whether findings reflect population-level risk changes or likely individual outcomes.
